questions.q: Which of the following units is equivalent to 1 lumen per square meter?
questions.n: Lux is the SI unit for illuminance, defined as one lumen per square meter.

questions.q: According to the NBC, what is the minimum required clearance between the underside of an elevator car and the bottom of the pit?
questions.n: The National Building Code specifies 600 mm as the safety buffer at the bottom of the elevator shaft.

questions.q: What mechanical device is an air-operated component used to open or close a damper or valve?
questions.n: An air motor uses compressed air to create mechanical motion, typically for controlling dampers.

questions.q: In a drainage system, how many stories must a waste stack serve before a parallel vent stack is required?
questions.n: Plumbing standards require a parallel vent stack when the waste stack serves 10 or more stories.

questions.q: Which term describes a graph used in air-conditioning to show the properties of air-system mixtures?
questions.n: This chart illustrates the relationships between dry-bulb temperature, humidity, and enthalpy.

questions.q: What is the maximum rated speed for an escalator along the angle of travel under the NBC?
questions.n: The National Building Code caps escalator speed at 38 meters per minute for passenger safety.

questions.q: In plumbing, what is the combination of pipe fittings typically installed at the base of a soil stack?
questions.n: This combination provides a gradual 45-degree transition that prevents clogging and solid accumulation.

questions.q: Which type of heat is responsible for raising the actual temperature of the air?
questions.n: Sensible heat can be 'sensed' or measured by a thermometer as a change in temperature.

questions.q: What is the term for a heavy conductor, usually a solid copper bar, used for collecting and distributing large electrical currents?
questions.n: A 'Bus' or 'Busbar' acts as a central junction for high-current electrical distribution.

questions.q: True or False: The effective room temperature range for air-conditioning is generally considered to be 68-74 degrees Fahrenheit.
questions.n: This range represents the standard thermal comfort zone used in mechanical climate control.

questions.q: Which term describes the rate of flow of light through a surface?
questions.n: This measures the total perceived power of light emitted by a source or passing through a surface.

questions.q: What is the equivalent of a filament in a fluorescent lamp?
questions.n: In a fluorescent lamp, the cathode is the electrode that emits electrons to sustain the discharge.

questions.q: In theater stage houses, what is the iron or sand weight used to balance suspended scenery called?
questions.n: Counterweights are used in rigging systems to offset the weight of sets, curtains, or lighting pipes.

questions.q: On elevators, what is the gear-driven machine having a drum to which the wire ropes are fastened and wound?
questions.n: In this system, the hoisting ropes are physically wrapped around a cylindrical drum to raise or lower the car.

questions.q: What is the NBC minimum width required between balusters in an escalator?
questions.n: The National Building Code sets 558 mm as the standard minimum width for the escalator interior.

questions.q: What is the term for a private telephone system that interconnects with public telephone systems?
questions.n: Private Automatic Branch Exchange systems allow internal switching and connection to the external public network.

questions.q: In an alternating current (AC) system, what is the total resistance called?
questions.n: Impedance combines standard resistance with reactive components in an AC circuit.

questions.q: What is the reciprocal of conductance?
questions.n: Resistance measures the opposition to current flow, making it the mathematical inverse of conductance.

questions.q: Which term refers to the rate of flow of sound energy?
questions.n: Sound intensity is defined as the power carried by sound waves per unit area in a direction perpendicular to that area.

questions.q: What type of lighting is used primarily to draw attention to particular points of interest?
questions.n: Accent lighting creates visual interest by highlighting specific objects or architectural features.

questions.q: A type of High-Intensity-Discharge (HID) lamp is:
questions.n: HPS lamps are a specific category of HID lamps known for their yellow-orange light.

questions.q: What sound system input device reacts to and converts variable sound pressure into variable electrical current?
questions.n: A microphone acts as a transducer, turning acoustic energy into an electrical signal.

questions.q: A thermal detector is what specific type of safety device?
questions.n: This type of thermal detector triggers an alarm when it senses a rapid increase in temperature.

questions.q: What is the term for light originating from sources not facing each other, such as from windows in adjacent walls?
questions.n: Cross light occurs when illumination comes from different angles, often creating balanced shadows.

questions.q: A louvered construction divided into cell-like areas used for redirecting light emitted by an overhead source is called:
questions.n: Eggcrates are common in lighting fixtures to reduce glare and control the direction of the light beam.

questions.q: A lamp designed to project and diffuse a uniform level of illumination over a large area is a:
questions.n: Floodlights are used to 'flood' a wide area with light, such as building facades or parking lots.

questions.q: In boilers, what components function only when conditions exceed prescribed unsafe operating limits?
questions.n: These are safety devices that shut down the system if pressure or temperature becomes dangerous.

questions.q: What type of sound absorbent is best for lower band frequencies?
questions.n: While porous absorbents vary, they are the category cited for handling lower frequencies in this context.

questions.q: The bending of a sound wave when traveling forward changes direction as it passes through different densities is called:
questions.n: Refraction is the change in direction caused by a change in the wave's speed through different densities.

questions.q: Which water distribution system relies constantly on pressure from the main water pipe and is applied only if the highest fixture is supplied continuously?
questions.n: This system uses the pressure from the municipal main to push water directly up to the fixtures.

questions.q: What is the mechanical equipment, coupled with a central air-conditioning system, used to dehumidify and cool the air stream injected into a space?
questions.n: A Fan Coil Unit (FCU) consists of a heating/cooling coil and a fan to condition local air.

questions.q: A rigid metal housing for a group of heavy conductors insulated from each other and the enclosure is called a:
questions.n: Also known as Busduct, it is used to distribute high-power electricity throughout a building.

questions.q: Which lighting system directs 90-100% of light output to the ceiling and upper walls of the room?
questions.n: Indirect lighting uses reflective surfaces like ceilings to scatter light, minimizing glare.

questions.q: What is the luminous intensity of any surface in a given direction per unit of projected area?
questions.n: Luminance describes the brightness of a surface as perceived by the eye.

questions.q: Which unit is equivalent to 1 lumen per square foot?
questions.n: The foot-candle is the imperial unit for illuminance, widely used in the US.

questions.q: What automatic device is used for converting high, fluctuating inlet water pressure to a lower constant pressure?
questions.n: This valve maintains a consistent downstream pressure regardless of upstream fluctuations.

questions.q: Under NBC, what is the minimum diameter of hoisting and counterweight rope?
questions.n: The code specifies 30 mm as the minimum thickness for these critical elevator cables.

questions.q: A means of producing light from gaseous discharge is known as:
questions.n: Fluorescence is the emission of light by a substance that has absorbed light or other electromagnetic radiation.

questions.q: Which term describes the process of removing calcium and magnesium deposits in water?
questions.n: Water softening specifically targets the 'hardness' minerals like calcium and magnesium.

questions.q: The transmission of heat energy from one place to another by circulatory movement of a mass of fluid is:
questions.n: Convection involves the physical movement of gases or liquids carrying heat.

questions.q: True or False: The equivalent of a filament in a fluorescent lamp is the Cathode.
questions.n: In discharge lamps, the cathode provides the electrons needed for light production, similar to a filament's role.

questions.q: Which specific unit is equivalent to 1 lumen per square foot?
questions.n: One foot-candle is defined as the amount of light on a one square foot surface from a uniform source.

questions.q: What is the maximum rated speed of an escalator along the angle of travel under NBC?
questions.n: National Building Codes typically limit escalator speed to 38 meters per minute for passenger safety.

questions.q: What is the term for the total opposition to alternating current flow?
questions.n: Impedance represents the vector sum of resistance and reactance in an AC circuit.

questions.q: True or False: Number of fixture units is one parameter in sizing a drainage pipe.
questions.n: Fixture units help estimate the potential load on the plumbing system to ensure pipes are large enough.

questions.q: Which device is air-operated and used to open or close a damper?
questions.n: An air motor uses pneumatic pressure to provide the mechanical motion required for dampers.

questions.q: What is the rating index of an air-conditioning system which rates the unit for the number of BTU's of heat removed per watt of electrical input energy?
questions.n: EER is a direct ratio of cooling capacity (BTU/hr) to electrical power input (Watts).

questions.q: Which term describes a heavy conductor, usually a solid copper bar, used for collecting and distributing large electrical currents?
questions.n: A 'Bus' or 'Busbar' acts as a high-current manifold for power distribution within a panel or switchgear.

questions.q: What unit is equivalent to 1 lumen per square meter?
questions.n: Lux is the standard international (SI) unit for illuminance.

questions.q: What is the material used for filament in an incandescent bulb?
questions.n: Tungsten has an extremely high melting point, allowing it to glow brightly without vaporizing quickly.

questions.q: Which device is used for converting high fluctuating inlet water pressure to a lower constant pressure?
questions.n: These valves protect plumbing fixtures from damage caused by high municipal water pressure.

questions.q: What type of HID lamp uses sodium as its primary gas for discharge?
questions.n: HPS lamps are highly efficient and produce a distinct golden-white light.

questions.q: In acoustics, what is the term for the bending of a sound wave when it passes through different densities?
questions.n: Refraction happens when sound waves speed up or slow down as they move through air of different temperatures or densities.

questions.q: True or False: A lighting unit consisting of one or more electrical lamps is called a Luminaire.
questions.n: A luminaire is the complete lighting fixture, including the lamps and all parts for distribution and connection.

questions.q: Which term describes the process of removing calcium and magnesium from water to prevent scale buildup?
questions.n: Water softening is the targeted removal of 'hardness' ions.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of stories served by a waste stack requiring a parallel vent stack?
questions.n: When a waste stack reaches 10 stories, a separate parallel stack is needed to manage pressure.

questions.q: Which graph shows the properties of air-system mixtures?
questions.n: This chart is the primary tool for understanding temperature and humidity relationships in air.

questions.q: What is the equivalent of a filament in a fluorescent lamp?
questions.n: The cathode is the component that glows and releases electrons to maintain the light.

questions.q: In AC systems, what is the term for total resistance including reactance?
questions.n: Impedance is the full vector sum of all resistive forces in an AC circuit.

questions.q: Under NBC, what is the minimum clearance between the underside of the elevator car and the bottom of the pit?
questions.n: NBC requires 600 mm of clearance to ensure safety for technicians in the pit.
